PASSED: Independently re-ran: full apps/api jest suite (15/15, incl. the 2 new health tests), pnpm typecheck + pnpm build clean, diff scope check clean (only health/ + app.module.ts + deploy.yml touched, no creep). Parsed deploy.yml with js-yaml to confirm it's still valid YAML and the single-quoted remote ssh script wasn't broken by the new bash block (no stray single quotes), then bash -n'd the extracted script for syntax. Live-verified the exact retry-loop logic on the actual production VPS (not just locally) against two real conditions: (1) closed port -> curl fails in ~15ms real time on the Linux box (my initial Windows/git-bash test showed a misleading ~2s-per-attempt artifact, ruled out as environment-specific, not a real issue); (2) against the currently-deployed (pre-this-feature) api container's real /api/health 404 -- loop correctly retried 15x and exited 1 after ~30s wall-clock, matching the code's own "after 30s" log message. No blocking findings.

PASSED: Reviewed health.controller.ts, health.module.ts, app.module.ts diff, and the deploy.yml change. No auth on GET /api/health is correct/intentional (health endpoints must be reachable by CI/monitoring without credentials) and leaks nothing sensitive -- response is a static {status:ok} or a generic 503 message, never the raw DB error. $queryRaw is a static parameterless literal (SELECT 1), zero injection surface -- no user input anywhere in this endpoint. Still covered by the existing global ThrottlerGuard, so it's not an unthrottled DoS vector. deploy.yml change adds no new secrets and doesn't touch existing secret handling; the curl target is a hardcoded 127.0.0.1 literal, no SSRF. No new npm dependency. Not applicable: IDOR, money/balance races, DTO validation (no request body/params exist). One non-blocking note: health.controller.ts's catch block discards the real Prisma error before throwing ServiceUnavailableException -- fine for the public response, but means ops has zero server-log signal for *why* health failed beyond docker/prisma logs elsewhere; recommend a Logger.warn(err) before the throw, same pattern as the existing non-blocking note on DOCS-001's users.service.ts. Not blocking.

COMPLETED: Read current main's User/Seller/Order models, auth.service.ts (register/login/changePassword/getMe/updateMe already exist!), users.service.ts SAFE_SELECT, and the full referrals.service.ts + admin referrals.tsx from the stale feature/sku-username-referrals branch. Plan: rename the branch's 'referralCode' concept to 'username' (schema field User.username, unique, auto-generated 8-char lowercase alphanumeric at registration with retry-loop, changeable via new PATCH endpoint). Critical cross-table uniqueness edge case identified and must be handled: Seller.handle (already on main, sellers' own referral code) and User.username are separate unique constraints on separate tables -- generation AND the new change-username endpoint must check BOTH tables to prevent a customer picking a username that collides with an existing seller handle (silent shadowing: resolveReferrerByUsername checks seller.handle first, so a colliding user username would never resolve to that user). New Referral model (PENDING/REWARDED/VOID lifecycle), ReferralSettings singleton, Order.referralDiscountTmt, race-safe discount application (conditional updateMany, not read-then-write) and idempotent reward-on-qualifying-order -- port directly from the branch's proven design. Admin referrals.tsx ports near-verbatim (settings/leaderboard/ledger UI already matches existing admin conventions). Do NOT port the branch's apps/seller extraction or seller-login-by-handle changes -- unrelated, out of scope, would conflict with this session's main.

COMPLETED: Ported and adapted the referral system: migration (username nullable->backfilled with own cuid id for existing rows->NOT NULL+unique, avoiding any collision risk; new Referral/ReferralSettings tables), referrals module (service/controller/DTOs), auth.service.ts register() now generates a username via ReferralsService and records the referral fire-and-forget, login/getMe/updateMe expose username. Wired into sellers.service.ts (seller's User.username = their handle, cross-checked against existing usernames in assertPhoneAndHandleFree) and users.service.ts (staff creation generates a username too) since username is now a required unique column on every User row. Orders integration: create() applies a race-safe referral-balance discount against amountTmt (recipient still gets full value, customer pays less), processTopup() rewards the referrer when the referee's order completes. 12 new unit tests (cross-table username collision, race-condition fallback to 409, discount capping, self-referral guard, disabled-program no-op) + full existing suite all green (39/39). Full monorepo typecheck clean. Live E2E verified via curl end-to-end: register with referral code -> stats show pending:1 -> complete referee's order -> reward credited (referralBalanceTmt +10) -> new order for referrer auto-discounts (verified exact math: 50 TMT - 10 balance = 40 TMT charged) -> balance drained to 0 -> username change tested (409 on collision with existing user, 200 on free name) -> admin ledger/leaderboard verified showing correct denormalized old username even after the referrer changed their username. Admin Referrals page ported, live-verified in browser rendering real data (settings values, leaderboard, ledger).

(2) Traced partner-API order path (apiKeyId-attributed, no userId): both the discount-application and reward-crediting code paths are guarded by /, so partner orders correctly skip referral logic entirely with no crash risk. (3) Confirmed RolesGuard uses getAllAndOverride, so the method-level @Roles('ADMIN') on the settings PATCH correctly overrides the controller-level @Roles('ADMIN','MANAGER') -- managers can view settings but only full admins can change reward amounts, matching the existing pattern used elsewhere in this codebase. (4) Re-ran full test suite independently (39/39) and full monorepo typecheck (clean). No blocking findings.

PASSED: Reviewed the full diff. No auth bypass: username-change endpoint requires JwtAuthGuard, operates only on the caller's own userId (no IDOR -- there is no id parameter accepted from the client for this mutation). Race conditions: applyReferralDiscount uses a conditional updateMany (gte check + decrement in one atomic statement), not read-then-write -- matches the pattern this codebase already required for money-touching code (Seller.balanceTmt precedent). changeUsername has a pre-check plus a P2002 catch as the real safety net against a concurrent-change race -- correct defense in depth. Injection: no raw SQL anywhere in the new code, all Prisma query builder. Input validation: class-validator on both new DTOs, username format enforced server-side via a regex (not just client-side), independent of whatever the admin UI or apps/web later send. Business logic abuse checks: self-referral blocked (referrerUserId === refereeUserId), a bad/garbage referral code at registration is swallowed in a try-catch so it can never DoS or fail signups, reward crediting is idempotent (checks status still PENDING before paying out, so re-processing an order or a retried queue job cannot double-pay). Data exposure: username is intentionally public/shareable (it's a referral code), no secret fields (passwordHash, tokenHash) touched by any new select clause. No blocking findings.

PASSED: Reviewed the diff. Avatar public GET is a deliberate design choice (documented in code comments), not an oversight -- avatars carry no secret data, and the storedName is a random UUID never derived from user input, validated by a strict regex before any filesystem access, so no path traversal and no enumeration beyond guessing UUIDs. Upload/delete require JwtAuthGuard and act only on req.user.userId -- no id parameter accepted from the client, so no IDOR is possible on either endpoint. Old avatar file is deleted only after the new DB row commits successfully; a failed DB write cleans up the orphaned new file instead of leaving one dangling -- verified by a dedicated test. Phone change reuses the exact same uniqueness-check-then-write pattern already established for username, self-exclusion correctly implemented so a user can PATCH without changing their own phone. No new auth bypass, no secret fields exposed in any new select clause. One accepted, explicitly-documented limitation carried over from the Document module's existing precedent: file-type filtering is by declared Content-Type header only, not actual content sniffing -- consistent with, not a regression from, the existing security posture. No blocking findings.
